Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:10:1.hebrew: התקדשי לי כו' - אם יש באחת מהן שוה פרוטה — מקודשת, ואם לאו — אין מצטרפין לש"פ. דכיון דאמר בכל חדא ״התקדשי״, כל חדא הוו קידושין באפי נפשייהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:10:1.english: Be betrothed to me, etc. - If there is the value of a peruta in one of them, she is betrothed; and if not, they do not combine to [reach] the value of a peruta. For since he said with each one, “Be betrothed,” each one was a betrothal on its own.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:10:2.hebrew: מאן תנא - דבעינן ״התקדשי״ ״התקדשי״, ואי לא אמר ״התקדשי״ לכל חדא, אלא ״התקדשי לי בזו ובזו״ — הוו מצטרפי לפרוטה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:10:2.english: Who is the tanna - [Who holds] that we require [him to say,] "Be betrothed," "Be betrothed," and that if he did not say "Be betrothed" for each one, but rather [said,] "Be betrothed to me with this and with that" — they would combine to [the value of] a peruta?

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:11:1.hebrew: ר"ש היא דאמר - גבי חמשה תובעין אותו, "תן לנו פקדון שיש בידך", ואמר, "שבועה שאין לך בידי, לא לך ולא לך" — אינו חייב אלא אחת, עד שיאמר שבועה לכל אחד ואחד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:11:1.english: It is Rabbi Shimon, who says - Regarding five [people who] claim from him: "Give us the deposit that is in your possession," and he said: "An oath that you have nothing in my possession, not to you and not to you" — he is liable for only one [offering], unless he says "an oath" to each and every one.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:12:1.hebrew: ובפרטי סבר לה כר"ש - דלא חשיב פרטא עד שיאמר לכל אחד ואחד שבועה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:12:1.english: And with regard to specification, he holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon - For it is not considered a specification until he says “an oath” to each and every one.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:13:1.hebrew: כלל אינו חייב אלא אחת - ובשבועות מפרש איזהו כללו של ר"מ ופרטו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:13:1.english: [If he] included, he is liable for only one - And in [tractate] Shevuot, [the Gemara] explains what is Rabbi Meir's general [denial] and his specific [denial].

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:13:2.hebrew: שבועה - שאין לך בידי, ולא לך, ולא לך, ולא לך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:13:2.english: An oath - That there is nothing of yours in my possession, nor of yours, nor of yours, nor of yours.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:13:3.english: He is liable - [To bring] a guilt-offering for robbery.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:13:4.hebrew: לא לך לא לך - דוקא בלא וי"ו, אבל ולא לך ולא לך — כללא הוי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:13:4.english: Not to you, not to you - [This applies] specifically without a vav, but [if he said,] “And not to you, and not to you,” it is a general statement [and he is liable for only one].

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:13:5.hebrew: לא לך ולא לך שבועה - דבעינן שבועה באחרונה, אבל אם הזכיר שבועה תחלה, לא שדינן אכולהו, וכללא הוי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:13:5.english: “Not to you and not to you, an oath” - For we require [the word] “an oath” at the end; but if he mentioned “an oath” at the beginning, we do not apply [the oath] to all of them, and it is a general statement.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:14:1.hebrew: אלא - מתני' ד״התקדשי התקדשי״ — ר"ש היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:14:1.english: Rather - The Mishnah of “Be betrothed, be betrothed” is according to Rabbi Shimon:

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:14:2.english: And with regard to agency he holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - That [it is] her father [who can appoint an agent], and not she.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:15:1.hebrew: אנא נמי לא הואי בי מדרשא אבל רבי אבין הוה בבי מדרשא - והוא אמר לי לאחר שיצא, שחברו כל חבורות של בית המדרש, ונמנו וגמרו כרבי יוחנן — דבקידושין אביה, ולא היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:15:1.english: I too was not in the study hall, but Rabbi Avin was in the study hall - And he told me after he came out that all the groups of the study hall joined together, and they voted and concluded in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan — that regarding betrothal, her father [accepts it], and not she.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:15:2.hebrew: כי כרוכיא - תרגום של עגור, גרוא"ה בלע"ז:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:15:2.english: Like a crane - [It is] the [Aramaic] translation of agur, [which is] grue [crane] in Old French.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:15:3.hebrew: ויצאה והיתה - כך היה צועק: הא כתיב ״ויצאה והיתה״ — הויה כיציאה: מה גירושין בין היא בין אביה, אף קידושין בין היא בין אביה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:15:3.english: And she departs… and becomes - This is what he was shouting: Behold, it is written: “And she departs… and becomes” — [equating] becoming [betrothal] to departure [divorce]: Just as regarding divorce, [it may be received] either by her or by her father, so too regarding betrothal, [it may be accepted] either by her or by her father.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:15:4.hebrew: אמר ליה ואבין בר סמכא הוא - בלשון שאילה קאמר ליה: ובקי אתה ברבי אבין זה, שיש לסמוך על דבריו, שמדקדק בשמועתו, שאינו משכח:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:15:4.english: He said to him: And is Avin reliable? - He said to him in the form of a question: "And are you familiar with this Rabbi Avin, that one can rely on his words — that he is meticulous in what he heard, [and] that he does not forget?"

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:15:5.hebrew: כמין ימא לטגני - לא היתה לו שהות שכחה בנתים, שכשיצא מבית המדרש אמרה לי מיד — כשולה דג מן הים, והמחבת נתונה על האור לתתו בתוכו בשמן לטגנו. טגני — פריזר"א בלע"ז:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:15:5.english: Like [from] the sea to the frying pan - He had no time to forget in the interim, for when he left the study hall, he told it to me immediately — like one who pulls a fish from the sea while the frying pan is [already] set upon the fire, to place it into it in oil to fry it. *Tignei* — *frizera* [frying pan] in Old French.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:16:1.hebrew: אנא לא ר' אבין ברבי חייא - בשמועה זו של ר' אבין, לא שמעתי איזה אבין הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:16:1.english: I [do] not [say]: Rabbi Avin, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya - In this tradition of Rabbi Avin, I did not hear which Avin he is.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:1:1.hebrew: קטנה - שהיא שומרת יבם מן האירוסין, דעדיין רשות אביה עליה כל זמן שלא השיאה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:1:1.english: A minor girl - Who is awaiting the levir from betrothal, for her father's authority is still over her as long as he has not given her in marriage.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:1:2.hebrew: והנערה בין מדעת אביה וכו' - אלמא היכא דמפקעת עצמה מרשות אב, קיימי נמי רבנן במילתייהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:1:2.english: And a young woman, either with the consent of her father, etc. - Evidently, where she removes herself from her father’s authority, the Rabbis also maintain their position.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:2:1.english: Betrothal, which [is] with consent - For we require the consent of the transferor.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:2:2.hebrew: אביה ולא היא - שהתורה זיכתה לו. אבל גירושין, שישנה בעל כרחה — בין היא בין אביה, דמה לנו לדעתו? כי מקבל ליה איהו נמי, על כרחיה הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:2:2.english: Her father and not her - For the Torah granted [this right] to him. But divorce, which can [take place] against her will — either she or her father [can receive it], for what does his consent matter to us? Even when he receives it, it is against his will.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:3:1.hebrew: ורבי היא - דאמר מאמר תופס ביבמה בעל כרחה, אם זרק לה כסף ואמר לה: ״הרי את מקודשת לי״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:3:1.english: And it is [in accordance with] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] - For he says that levirate betrothal [ma’amar] takes effect on a yevama against her will, if he threw money to her and said to her: “Behold, you are betrothed to me.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:3:2.hebrew: רבי אמר קנה - כשאר מאמר, להיות צריכה גט למאמר זה, אם בא לחלוץ לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:3:2.english: Rabbi said: He acquires [her] - [He acquires her] like any other levirate betrothal, in that she requires a bill of divorce for this levirate betrothal if he comes to perform chalitzah with her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:4:1.hebrew: ביאה - דיבמה קניא לה בעל כרחה, דנפקא לן מויבמה בפ"ק דיבמות (דף ח:):
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:4:1.english: Intercourse - [Intercourse] with a yevama acquires her against her will, as we derive from “veyibmah” [“and consummate the levirate marriage with her”] in the first chapter of Yevamot (8b).

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:6:1.hebrew: וה"נ מסתברא - דהא דקתני גבי מאמר "בין היא בין אביה", במאמר על כרחה קאי, אבל בשאר קידושין — אביה ולא היא, כר' יוחנן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:6:1.english: And so too, it is reasonable - For that which [the baraita] teaches regarding levirate betrothal, "either she or her father," refers to levirate betrothal [performed] against her will; but with regard to other betrothals, [it is] her father and not she, in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:6:2.hebrew: מדקתני סיפא - בההיא: והנערה, בין מדעת אביה בין מדעת עצמה, מה שאין כן בקידושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:6:2.english: From the fact that it teaches in the latter clause - In that [baraita]: "And a young woman, whether with her father's consent or with her own consent, unlike in betrothal."

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:6:3.hebrew: ההיא ר' יהודה היא - וא"ת: במאמר מ"ט מודה, ומ"ש מאמר מגירושין — הרי שניהם על כרחה? לקמיה פריך לה, ומשני: שכן זקוקה ועומדת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:6:3.english: That [baraita] is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda - And if you say: In [the case of] levirate betrothal [ma’amar], what is the reason [Rabbi Yehuda] concedes, and in what way is levirate betrothal different from divorce — behold, both of them [can take effect] against her will? — later on, [the Gemara] poses this [difficulty] and resolves [it]: For she is already bound [to the yavam] and standing [in wait for him].

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:7:1.hebrew: מה שאין כן בגירושין מיבעי ליה - ואפילו בגירושין, דאיתנהו בעל כרחה, פליג ר' יהודה נמי, ואמר: "אין שתי ידים זוכות כאחת":
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:7:1.english: "Unlike with regard to divorce," it should have [stated] - And even regarding divorce, which can [take place] against her will, Rabbi Yehuda also disagrees and says: "Two hands do not acquire as one."

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:8:1.hebrew: מ"ש מאמר - כיון דבגירושין פליג, דאיתנייהו בעל כרחה — ומ"ש מאמר דמודה בה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:8:1.english: In what way is levirate betrothal different - Since [Rabbi Yehuda] disagrees with regard to divorce, which can [take place] against her will — in what way is levirate betrothal different, that he concedes with regard to it?

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:8:2.english: Since she is bonded and standing - Therefore, [levirate betrothal] takes effect upon her through any [means] whatsoever.

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:8:3.hebrew: השתא דאתית להכי - דתלית טעמא משום דזקוקה ועומדת, לרבי יוחנן נמי — לטעמיה קמא דיהיב רבי יוחנן למלתייהו דרבנן: דגירושין מכנסת עצמה לרשות אביה, וקידושין מפקעת עצמה, ואותיבנא ממאמר דמפקעת עצמה — לא תיקשי; דאיכא לשנויי נמי: שאני מאמר, הואיל וזקוקה ועומדת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:8:3.english: Now that you have arrived at this - That you have based the reason on [the fact] that she is bonded and standing [in wait] — for Rabbi Yoḥanan as well, regarding his first reason that Rabbi Yoḥanan gave for the position of the Rabbis: that [in the case of] divorce she brings herself into her father’s authority, and [in the case of] betrothal she removes herself [from her father's authority], and we raised an objection from levirate betrothal, [where] she removes herself — [this] should not pose a difficulty; for it can also be answered: Levirate betrothal is different, since she is bonded and standing [in wait].

Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:9:1.hebrew: בה ובשלוחה לא - אלמא נערה שיש לה אב לא מקדשה עצמה, וקס"ד דברי הכל היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 44a:9:1.english: By herself or by her agent, no - Consequently, a young woman who has a father cannot betroth herself, and [the Gemara] assumed that it is [the opinion of] all.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 44a:13:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר שבועה לא לך לא לך חייב על כל אחת - כך גירסת הקונט', ופי': דבענין זה הוי פרטא; אבל אמר: "שבועה לא לך ולא לך" — כללא הוי, ואינו חייב אלא אחת, דוי"ו מוסיף על ענין ראשון. ור"ת גורס איפכא: דאדרבה, כשאומר "ולא לך ולא לך" — משמע שהוא נשבע לכל אחד; אבל כשאומר "לא לך לא לך" — אינו חייב אלא אחת:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 44a:13:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: “An oath: Not to you, not to you,” he is liable for each and every one - This is the reading of the Kuntres [Rashi], and he explained that in this manner it is a specification; but if he said: “An oath: Not to you and not to you,” it is a general statement, and he is liable for only one [offering], for a [letter] vav connects to the preceding matter. And Rabbeinu Tam reads the opposite: for on the contrary, when he says “and not to you, and not to you,” it implies that he is taking an oath to each one; but when he says “not to you, not to you,” he is liable for only one.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 44a:15:1.hebrew: צווח ר"ל ויצאה והיתה - ואע"ג דאפילו ר"ל לא מקיש הויה ליציאה — שהרי בקטנה היא מתגרשת, אף ע"י עצמה לרבנן, אם יש לה דעת לשמור גיטה, ואינה מתקדשת על ידי עצמה — מ"מ יש לנו להשוותם בכל מה שנוכל מלשון ״ויצאה והיתה״; א"כ, אין לנו לחלק בין קידושין לגירושין בנערה. דנהי נמי דמחלקין גבי קטנה — היינו משום שאין לה יד לקבל קידושין, אבל לקבל גיטה יש לה יד, כיון שנשאת:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 44a:15:1.english: Reish Lakish screamed: “And she departs… and becomes” - And even though even Reish Lakish does not equate becoming [betrothal] to departure [divorce] — for behold, in [the case of] a minor girl, she may be divorced even by herself according to the Rabbis if she has the understanding to safeguard her bill of divorce, yet she cannot be betrothed by herself — nevertheless, we must equate them in whatever [aspect] we can, from the phrase “and she departs… and becomes.” If so, we should not differentiate between betrothal and divorce in [the case of] a young woman. For although indeed we differentiate in the case of a minor girl, that is because she has no hand [i.e., legal capacity] to receive betrothal, but to receive her bill of divorce she does have a hand, since she was married.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 44a:15:2.hebrew: כמין ימא לטיגני - פי' בקונטרס: לא היתה שהות שכחה בנתים, כמו שולה דגים מן הים והמחבת נתונה על האור לתתן בתוכה בשמן לטגנן. ור"ח פירש: דשני מקומות הם וקרובים זה לזה, כלומר: אין אדם משקר כה"ג, דכיון דמקום קרוב הוא, סבר: ״אי משקרנא — אתי אינש אחרינא ומכחישני״; הילכך לא משקר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 44a:15:2.english: Like from the sea to the frying pan - The Kuntres Rashi explained: There was no interim time for forgetting, like one who hauls fish from the sea while the frying pan is set upon the fire to place them into it in oil to fry them. And Rabbeinu Chananel explained that they are two places and close to one another; that is to say: A person does not lie in a case like this, for since it is a nearby place, he reasons: “If I lie, another person will come and contradict me”; therefore, he does not lie.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 44a:3:1.hebrew: במאמר דבע"כ ורבי היא - וא"ת: א"כ, מאי קאמר: "קטנה אין עושין בה מאמר אלא מדעת אביה, והנערה מדעתה ומדעת אביה"? ואי כרבי, הא לא בעינן לא דעתה ולא דעת אביה! וי"ל, דהכי קאמר: צריך להודיע לה או לאביה, ואח"כ יקדשנה בעל כרחה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 44a:3:1.english: "With levirate betrothal against her will, and it is [in accordance with] Rabbi" - And if you say: If so, why does it state: “A minor girl — one may perform levirate betrothal on her only with the consent of her father, and a young woman — [either] with her consent or with the consent of her father”? For if [it is] in accordance with Rabbi, behold, we require neither her consent nor her father's consent! And one can say that this is what it means: He must inform her or her father, and afterwards he may betroth her against her will.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 44a:8:1.hebrew: מאי שנא מאמר - פירו': אמאי מחלק מאמר מגירושין? אי משום דמאמר בע"כ — גירושין נמי בע"כ נינהו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 44a:8:1.english: "In what way is levirate betrothal different" - Explanation: Why does [Rabbi Yehuda] distinguish levirate betrothal from divorce? If [it is] because levirate betrothal [takes effect] against her will — divorce also [takes effect] against her will.
